title: Authorities seize Polk County residence following 16 narcotics arrests - NewsBreak
text: POLK COUNTY, Texas ( KETK ) — A Polk County residence was seized by officials after four people were arrested for meth possession on Tuesday, totaling at least 16 narcotics arrest at the property in the last four years. The Polk County Sheriff’s Office carried out a search warrant at a residence in the Southland Plantation area, leading to the arrest of Lou Ann Hudson. At the time of her arrest, Hudson had two active felony warrants related to possession and manufacture or delivery of a controlled substance. During Hudson’s arrest, officials observed five other people and allegedly found a glass pipe commonly used to smoke methamphetamine in plain view at the residence. After a probable cause search warrant was obtained, officials uncovered more than four grams, but less than 200 grams of methamphetamine in Hudson’s bedroom. Another baggie holding less than one gram of methamphetamine was found inside a different room, the sheriff’s said, that was occupied by Sherry Saunders, Ginger Richards and James Robert Pipkin. All three occupants denied owning the baggie and were later arrested on possession of a controlled substance less than one gram. Officials also administered a VIN check on a Dodge Ram pickup truck that did not possess any tires or engine. The truck was confirmed stolen from San Jacinto County and was given to the respective authorities for investigation, according to the sheriff’s office. Part of this investigation noted that the residence where this incident occurred has been the site of at least 16 narcotics related arrests spanning over four years. The frequent arrests of both users and dealers led officials to seize the property. “Due to the continued sale of illegal narcotics from the location and the persistent presence of drug users, the Narcotics Division has initiated civil seizure proceedings on the property in accordance with Chapter 59 of the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure,” officials said.
